recommended_intro: Kozyrskiy et al. benchmarked CSP- and covariance-based pipelines under time-ordered, label-revealed prequential evaluation across four EEG datasets [@kozyrskiy2026updates]. Their expanding- and rolling-history schemes refitted complete pipelines after each newly revealed trial, addressing update timing, memory and cold-start calibration. Here, each target session receives one fixed source-plus-current-support fit before the later whole runs are scored. The full-refit and classifier-only arms use identical source and current-session trial identities and identical query trials. Their difference quantifies the added spatial-representation update after the classifier has already received the same calibration labels.
recommended_probability_heading: Posterior covariance changed probability scores and classification differently
recommended_score_sentence: Across the fixed synthetic grid, adding posterior predictive covariance to identical posterior means reduced mean cross entropy by0.341 and Brier score by0.00191, while BA changed by−0.04points. In the EEG comparison, the same predictive step lowered BA and increased Brier score. These outcomes distinguish probability scoring from classification performance.
